housing.summary: Sydney is Australia's most expensive rental market. A 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre (CBD) typically rents for approximately AUD 600–700 per week. The standard bond (deposit) is 4 weeks rent, as regulated by NSW Fair Trading. Primary rental portals are realestate.com.au and domain.com.au.

banking.summary: To open a bank account in Australia, new arrivals typically need a valid passport, proof of Australian address, and a Tax File Number (TFN). CommBank allows account opening up to 14 days before arrival and accepts new migrants within 12 months of arrival with in-branch ID verification. ANZ and NAB also offer accounts for new residents.
required_docs: Valid passport (original required for in-branch ID verification within 20 days)

schools.summary: Sydney has a wide range of international schools offering IB (International Baccalaureate), British curriculum, and American curriculum. The national school directory myschool.edu.au lists all Australian schools including international-curriculum institutions.

legal_admin.summary: Visa holders in Australia must notify the Department of Home Affairs (Home Affairs) of any address changes. New residents should register with myGov (my.gov.au) to link essential government services including the ATO (tax), Medicare, and Centrelink.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register with myGov; notify Home Affairs of address changes

tax_finance.summary: All workers and income earners in Australia require a Tax File Number (TFN) from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). You can apply for a TFN online for free at ato.gov.au. The TFN is used by employers for payroll tax and by the ATO for income tax returns.

transport.summary: Sydney's public transport is operated by Transport for NSW using the Opal card system (tap-on/tap-off). Fares are distance-based with a weekly travel cap applying after 8 paid journeys. The Opal daily cap and weekly cap provide cost savings for frequent travellers. Overseas licence holders may drive in NSW on their overseas licence; exchange to an NSW licence is required after becoming a NSW resident (no fixed time limit but must be done when intending to reside permanently). Medicare registration for eligible visa holders is via Services Australia (servicesaustralia.gov.au).
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Overseas licence holders can drive in NSW on their foreign licence; must exchange to an NSW driver licence upon becoming a NSW resident. Exchange via Service NSW with identity documents, overseas licence, and eye test.
transport.healthcare_registration: Eligible visa holders enrol in Medicare at Services Australia offices or online via servicesaustralia.gov.au/medicare.
